guide.title: Steakhouses in Chicago: Twenty Rooms Between the River and Rush Street
guide.intro: Twenty rooms on this page, and every one of them inside the city limits. Half of them stand in River North, most within a few blocks of the Chicago River: Bavette's and RPM Steak both stand on West Kinzie Street, a block and a half apart, Gene & Georgetti holds the Franklin Street corner, Chicago Cut takes the water at 300 North LaSalle, and Mastro's, the Chicago Chop House, Kinzie Chophouse, Smith & Wollensky, Steak 48 and Fogo de Chão fill in around them. Six more sit on the Gold Coast and the Magnificent Mile, from Gibsons on Rush Street to the Capital Grille on North St. Clair. Four hold the Loop and the West Loop, with Swift & Sons out in Fulton Market where the meat trade used to be. Three Korean steakhouses qualify under the same rule and are published on the Chicago Korean barbecue guide, linked below.

sections.heading: River North
sections.body:
Ten of the twenty rooms sit in one neighborhood, and most of them are walkable from each other.

Bavette's Bar & Boeuf is on West Kinzie Street, a Hogsalt room of exposed brick and low light where the dry-aged rib eye is the cut the kitchen is built around. RPM Steak is a block and a half east at 66 West Kinzie, bringing a chef-driven menu to a traditional steakhouse list. Gene & Georgetti is on North Franklin Street and has been since 1941, per the city's own visitor listing, still run by the Durpetti family and still putting prime aged steaks beside chicken Vesuvio.

Chicago Cut Steakhouse takes the river frontage at 300 North LaSalle, a window-lined room with a patio on the water; the Michelin Guide's listing records that the beef is butchered and dry-aged on the premises, and the wine list arrives on a tablet you can search by varietal. The Chicago Chop House is around the corner on West Ontario in a Victorian brownstone built in 1897, according to the restaurant's own description, hand-cutting USDA Prime. Kinzie Chophouse opened on North Wells Street in 1991, is independently woman-owned, and calls itself an American steakhouse with a Mediterranean heartbeat.

Mastro's is on North Dearborn with live music every night and three second-floor private rooms that combine. Smith & Wollensky occupies a two-story building on North State Street with the river below it, Wollensky's Grill downstairs, and tours of the dry-aging room and butcher shop on request. Steak 48 is on North Wabash behind a glass-walled show kitchen. Fogo de Chão is on North LaSalle Drive, where the churrasco grill feeds a dining room seating more than three hundred.

sections.heading: The Gold Coast and the Magnificent Mile
sections.body:
Six rooms north and east of the river, strung along Rush Street and Michigan Avenue.

Gibsons Bar & Steakhouse is the Rush Street anchor at 1028 North Rush, and the group holds its own USDA Prime certification, according to the city's visitor listing. Maple & Ash is a block west on West Maple Street, where everything runs through open fire — even the seafood tower is fire-roasted rather than iced. Rosebud Steakhouse is on East Walton Place just off Michigan Avenue, working a prime New York sirloin and a Chicago-cut bone-in ribeye.

Michael Jordan's Steak House is at 505 North Michigan Avenue with steakhouse classics on a seasonal menu. The Capital Grille is on North St. Clair Street in Streeterville, a dry-aged house with an award-winning wine list. Joe's Seafood, Prime Steak & Stone Crab is on East Grand Avenue in the North Bridge blocks, carrying the Miami stone crab menu alongside the prime steaks.

sections.heading: The Loop and the West Loop
sections.body:
Four rooms, two on each side of the river's south branch.

Prime & Provisions holds the corner of North LaSalle and Wacker Drive across twelve thousand square feet, from the ground floor up to a second-floor dining room over the water, fitted out as a 1920s supper club and cutting its steaks by hand. Morton's The Steakhouse is a few blocks east on East Wacker Place, serving USDA prime-aged beef in a club-like room; the original Morton's at 1050 North State Street closed in November 2020 and this is the Chicago room that remains.

West of the river, Gibsons Italia opened on North Canal Street in October 2017 as the group's first downtown room in more than a decade — three levels, two fireplaces and a retractable roof over the river, with chef José Sosa running Italian dishes beside the beef. Swift & Sons is deeper into Fulton Market at 1000 West Fulton, built by the Boka Restaurant Group and B. Hospitality with chef Chris Pandel and designers AvroKO, in the district where the American meat trade did its business.

sections.heading: The three Korean steakhouses, published next door
sections.body:
Three Chicago rooms qualify under this collection's rule as Korean-style beef rooms, and all three already have place pages on the Chicago Korean barbecue guide.

Iron Age Korean Steakhouse in Wicker Park, Perilla Steakhouse on North Wabash Avenue and Shinhwa Korean Steakhouse on South Wentworth Avenue are beef rooms first, which is the same ground that puts COTE on the Manhattan page. A room is published once on this site, so this page names them and points at the guide that carries them. Iron Age's Glenview room is a north-suburbs address and is outside the scope of this page entirely.

faq.question: What makes a room a steakhouse on this page?
faq.answer: Steak has to be the menu's center of gravity, plus the beef-centric genres — churrascaria, Argentine parrilla, Japanese wagyu counter, Korean-style beef room. That rule keeps some well-liked Chicago rooms off the list. La Grande Boucherie on North Dearborn is an Art Nouveau Parisian brasserie with large-format meats on a French menu, which is a brasserie rather than a chophouse. Outback, LongHorn and Texas Roadhouse are casual national chains rather than destination rooms.

faq.question: Why do national chains like Morton's and the Capital Grille count when Outback does not?
faq.answer: The line is between national fine-dining steakhouses and national casual chains. Capital Grille, Morton's, Smith & Wollensky, Mastro's, Fogo de Chão and Steak 48 are steakhouses under the rule and each outpost is its own room with its own street and its own kitchen. Outback, LongHorn and Texas Roadhouse are not destination rooms and none of them appears anywhere in this collection.

faq.question: Which Morton's is the one on this page?
faq.answer: The room at 65 East Wacker Place in the Loop. The original Morton's at 1050 North State Street on the Gold Coast closed in November 2020, which Crain's Chicago Business and the local television stations all reported at the time, and the Wacker Place room stayed open. Same brand, different address, one room on this page.

faq.question: Why is there no suburban section?
faq.answer: Because the count did not need one. Chicago's steakhouse mass never left River North, the Gold Coast, the Loop and the West Loop, so twenty rooms inside the city limits carry the page on their own and Gibsons Oak Brook and Gibsons Rosemont are not required. That is the opposite of what happened to Chicago's Korean barbecue, where the grills moved out to Niles and Glenview and needed a second page.

faq.question: Why are Iron Age, Perilla and Shinhwa not listed as rooms here?
faq.answer: All three qualify as Korean-style beef rooms, and all three already have place pages on the Chicago Korean barbecue guide. A room is published once on this site, so this page names them in prose and links to the guide that carries them.

photos.title: 300 North LaSalle Street, Chicago
photos.description: A glass-and-steel office tower photographed steeply upward from street level against a deep blue sky, sunlight flaring off one face of the curtain wall, a smaller pale high-rise showing at the lower right and thin cloud at the edges of the frame. This is 300 North LaSalle, the building Chicago Cut Steakhouse occupies at river level.
photos.author: Gdefreitas

places.name: Bavette's Bar & Boeuf
places.summary: Bavette's is a Hogsalt steakhouse on West Kinzie Street in River North, a low-lit room of exposed brick and leather seating. The dry-aged rib eye is the cut the kitchen is built around.

places.name: Gene & Georgetti
places.summary: Gene & Georgetti is a River North chophouse on North Franklin Street putting prime aged steaks beside Italian dishes and chicken Vesuvio. The dining room has been on this corner a long time and the family still runs it.
places.history: Established in 1941 by Gene Michelotti and Alfredo Federighi, nicknamed Georgetti, according to the city's own visitor listing, and still operated by the Durpetti family.

places.name: Chicago Cut Steakhouse
places.summary: Chicago Cut takes the river frontage at 300 North LaSalle, a window-lined dining room with a patio on the water. The beef is butchered and dry-aged on the premises, per the Michelin Guide's listing, and the wine list arrives on a tablet you can search by varietal and country.

places.name: Gibsons Bar & Steakhouse
places.summary: Gibsons is the Rush Street anchor of Gold Coast steakhouse dining, taking parties from a dozen up to five hundred. The group holds its own USDA Prime certification, according to the city's visitor listing.

places.name: Gibsons Italia
places.summary: Gibsons Italia is the group's Italian steakhouse on North Canal Street in the West Loop, three levels with two fireplaces and a retractable roof over the river and the skyline. Chef José Sosa runs handmade pasta and risotto alongside the prime beef.
places.history: Opened in October 2017 as the Gibsons Restaurant Group's first downtown room in more than a decade.

places.name: Swift & Sons
places.summary: Swift & Sons is a modern American steakhouse in Fulton Market, the West Loop district built on the meat trade. It was created by the Boka Restaurant Group and B. Hospitality with executive chef Chris Pandel and the designers AvroKO.

places.name: RPM Steak
places.summary: RPM Steak sits on West Kinzie Street in River North and brings a chef-driven kitchen to a traditional steakhouse list. There is a bar and lounge in front of the dining room and private rooms behind it.

places.name: Maple & Ash
places.summary: Maple & Ash is a Gold Coast steakhouse where the open fire is the whole argument — the kitchen says its food tastes better cooked over one. Even the seafood tower is fire-roasted rather than iced, and the steaks come off the same hearth.

places.name: Steak 48
places.summary: Steak 48's Chicago room is on North Wabash Avenue behind a glass-enclosed show kitchen you can watch from the floor. USDA Prime steaks and Japanese Wagyu are the menu, with a second-floor outdoor patio above it.

places.name: Prime & Provisions
places.summary: Prime & Provisions holds twelve thousand square feet at North LaSalle and Wacker Drive, running from the ground floor to a second-floor dining room over the Chicago River. The steaks are hand-cut and the room is fitted out after a 1920s supper club.

places.name: Chicago Chop House
places.summary: The Chicago Chop House is on West Ontario Street in River North, hand-cutting USDA Prime steaks in house and running live music through the dining room. It occupies a Victorian brownstone built in 1897, according to the restaurant's own description.

places.name: Kinzie Chophouse
places.summary: Kinzie Chophouse is an independently woman-owned room on North Wells Street that calls itself an American steakhouse with a Mediterranean heartbeat. Its prime cuts come from Meats by Linz, a supply relationship the restaurant says has run more than thirty years.
places.history: Opened in 1991 and trading on the same River North corner ever since.

places.name: Rosebud Steakhouse
places.summary: Rosebud Steakhouse is on East Walton Place in the Gold Coast, a block east of Michigan Avenue. The prime New York sirloin and the Chicago-cut bone-in ribeye are the two cuts the menu is built on.

places.name: Michael Jordan's Steak House
places.summary: Michael Jordan's Steak House is on North Michigan Avenue at the foot of the Magnificent Mile, running steakhouse classics on a local and seasonal menu.

places.name: Smith & Wollensky
places.summary: The Chicago Smith & Wollensky is a two-story building on North State Street with the river underneath it and a seasonal patio outside. USDA Prime steaks are the menu, Wollensky's Grill runs on the lower level, and the restaurant will take you through the dry-aging room and the butcher shop on request.

places.name: Mastro's Steakhouse
places.summary: Mastro's Chicago room is on North Dearborn Street with live music every evening. Three private dining rooms on the second floor seat thirty-two apiece and combine for larger parties, above a steakhouse menu of signature cuts.

places.name: Morton's The Steakhouse
places.summary: Morton's Chicago room is on East Wacker Place in the Loop, a club-like dining room serving USDA prime-aged beef and seafood. Valet is among the room's own listed amenities, according to the city's own visitor listing.
places.history: The original Morton's at 1050 North State Street on the Gold Coast closed in November 2020, and this Wacker Place room is the one that continued.

places.name: The Capital Grille
places.address: 633 N St Clair St, Chicago, IL 60611
places.summary: The Capital Grille's Chicago room is on North St. Clair Street in Streeterville. Dry-aged steaks and an award-winning wine list are what the house is built on.

places.name: Joe's Seafood, Prime Steak & Stone Crab
places.summary: Joe's is on East Grand Avenue in the North Bridge blocks of River North, carrying the Miami stone crab menu — the claws, the signature sides, the key lime pie — alongside prime steaks. Five meeting rooms sit behind the dining room.

places.name: Fogo de Chão
places.summary: Fogo de Chão's River North churrascaria is on North LaSalle Drive, with a dining room seating more than three hundred around a white Carrara marble market table. Gaucho chefs fire-roast the beef and carve it at the table.

entries.name: Bavette's Bar & Boeuf
entries.note: West Kinzie Street, River North. The dry-aged rib eye is the signature cut.

entries.name: Gene & Georgetti
entries.note: North Franklin Street. The Italian half of the menu is not a garnish — chicken Vesuvio sits beside the prime aged steaks.

entries.name: Chicago Cut Steakhouse
entries.note: 300 North LaSalle, on the river. Ask about the in-house butchery; the tablet wine list is searchable by winery location.

entries.name: Gibsons Bar & Steakhouse
entries.note: 1028 North Rush Street. The Gold Coast room that gave Rush Street its steakhouse reputation.

entries.name: Gibsons Italia
entries.note: North Canal Street, West Loop. Three levels and a retractable roof; ask for the river side.

entries.name: Swift & Sons
entries.note: 1000 West Fulton Market. The steakhouse the West Loop got once Fulton Market stopped being a meat district and started being a dining one.

entries.name: RPM Steak
entries.note: 66 West Kinzie Street, River North. A block and a half east of Bavette's on the same street.

entries.name: Maple & Ash
entries.note: West Maple Street, Gold Coast. The fire-roasted seafood tower is the dish that tells you what the kitchen is doing.

entries.name: Steak 48
entries.note: North Wabash Avenue. Sit where you can see the glass show kitchen; the patio is on the second floor.

entries.name: Prime & Provisions
entries.note: LaSalle at Wacker. The second-floor dining room is the one over the river.

entries.name: Chicago Chop House
entries.note: West Ontario Street. A brownstone with live music, and every steak hand-cut on site.

entries.name: Kinzie Chophouse
entries.note: 400 North Wells Street. Greek hospitality on an American chophouse menu, and the same beef supplier for three decades.

entries.name: Rosebud Steakhouse
entries.note: East Walton Place. Small enough to feel like a neighborhood room a block off Michigan Avenue.

entries.name: Michael Jordan's Steak House
entries.note: 505 North Michigan Avenue. The Magnificent Mile address on this page, at the north end of the bridge.

entries.name: Smith & Wollensky
entries.note: North State Street, on the river. Wollensky's Grill downstairs is the later, looser half of the same building.

entries.name: Mastro's Steakhouse
entries.note: North Dearborn Street. Live music nightly, and the second floor is where the private rooms are.

entries.name: Morton's The Steakhouse
entries.note: East Wacker Place, the Loop. This is the Chicago Morton's — the State Street original is gone.

entries.name: The Capital Grille
entries.note: North St. Clair Street, Streeterville. The quiet end of the Magnificent Mile cluster.

entries.name: Joe's Seafood, Prime Steak & Stone Crab
entries.note: East Grand Avenue. Stone crab claws flown from Miami on the same table as the prime steak.

entries.name: Fogo de Chão
entries.note: North LaSalle Drive. The churrascaria on the page, with the market table anchored in front of the grill.

links.note: Iron Age Wicker Park, Perilla and Shinhwa are Korean-style beef rooms that qualify here, but their place pages publish on the Chicago Korean barbecue guide.
